result.title: How Network Topology and Data Heterogeneity Shape Decentralized Learning: A Spectral Analysis
result.summary: Network topology influences decentralized federated learning through information mixing and the relative contribution of individual nodes. While existing analyses primarily focus on spectral mixing properties, they often assume doubly stochastic aggregation, overlooking topology-dependent influence under irregular communication networks. We develop a spectral framework that separates two complementary mechanisms: the dominant eigenmode determines the consensus trajectory and node influence, while non-dominant eigenmodes govern the propagation and attenuation of disagreement. Under uniform neighborhood averaging, we show that the stationary influence is proportional to node degree plus one and derive a bound relating model disagreement to spectral mixing and gradient heterogeneity. We then investigate how these mechanisms interact with the data distribution across nodes. Experiments across regular and heterogeneous network topologies reveal nearly identical learning dynamics under IID data, while network size and connectivity affect how unevenly distributed information is learned under non-IID data. For non-IID settings, we characterize how the distribution of data across nodes shapes the relative contribution of local information to consensus dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建谱分析框架研究去中心化联邦学习：将聚合算子分解为主导特征模态（决定共识轨迹与节点影响力，均匀平均下稳态影响正比于「节点度+1」）与非主导模态（刻画分歧的传播与衰减），并结合数据异构性分析拓扑规模与连通度如何改变局部信息的相对贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按特征模态区分「共识收敛」与「分歧衰减」的谱刻画，可能为 latent 推理中跨迭代或跨层的状态混合、信息坍缩与证据权重分配提供可核查的分析工具，但研究对象是去中心化 FL 聚合，与 VLM 推理仅有间接概念联系。
